title: TnSeq and TRANSIT as a genome-wide essentiality assay
dek: Himar1 inserts at TA dinucleotides. A saturated library turns insertion density into a fitness map. TRANSIT is the analysis stack (Gumbel, HMM, resampling) — not a DST catalogue.
story: Transposon sequencing (TnSeq) asks, at genome scale, which loci tolerate insertion. In M. tuberculosis the workhorse is Himar1, which inserts at TA dinucleotides. H37Rv carries on the order of 74,000 TA sites. A saturated library — many independent insertions per TA, across a large pool — makes the absence of reads at a site informative rather than a sampling zero.

After outgrowth (7H10, macrophage, mouse spleen, a drug at sub-MIC), you sequence the insertion junctions. Genes that drop out of the pool are candidate essentials or condition-essentials. Genes that stay densely inserted are dispensable in that condition. This is a relative fitness assay on a pool, not a MIC and not a WHO catalogue grade.

TRANSIT (DeJesus, Ioerger and colleagues) is the usual analysis environment: Gumbel methods for essentiality of a whole gene, HMM models that can call domain-level essential segments inside a gene, and resampling tests for conditioned libraries. The software does not know your medium. A “non-essential” call on rich plates is compatible with essentiality in hypoxia or in a mouse.
deepTitle: What a computational lab actually checks
deep: Saturation first. A gene with two TA sites cannot be called essential by the same rule as a 40-TA gene. TRANSIT reports help; a methods section that omits library density is incomplete.

Read counts are compositional. A bottleneck (mouse infection, a harsh macrophage) inflates apparent essentiality because many insertions are lost by chance. Resampling and HMM help; they do not replace a bottleneck diagnostic (unique-insertion counts, occupancy).
Polar effects: an insertion can knock down a downstream gene in an operon. Essentiality of RvXXXX may be an operon artefact. CRISPRi and complementation are how you argue the gene rather than the TA.
TraSH and earlier microarray insertion methods are ancestors. Do not meta-analyse a 2003 TraSH list with a 2020 Himar1 HMM as if they were one likelihood.

Clinical WGS: a frameshift in a TnSeq-essential gene in a viable isolate is a mapping problem, a mixed sample, a wrong essentiality prior, or a condition mismatch — look at the BAM before you invent new biology.

formulas.label: Site occupancy (schematic)
formulas.expression: occupancy ≈ (# TA sites with ≥1 insertion) / (TA sites in window)
formulas.note: Near-zero occupancy along a gene is the essentiality signal after you have saturation.

visual.caption: Schematic TA map of a 900-bp gene. Dense insertions in the C-terminal third (dispensable in this condition) versus a cold N-terminal domain. HMM essentiality is a segment call, not a gene-name binary. TRANSIT is how you compute that; the wet library is how it is true.

example.title: Zero insertions in a 4-TA gene
example.setup: A 180-bp gene has four TA sites and zero insertions in a library whose genome-wide occupancy is ~50%. A student calls it “essential, p very small.” TRANSIT Gumbel on long genes in the same library looks well calibrated.

steps.title: Under-powered window
steps.body: Four sites at 50% occupancy can be empty by chance with probability 0.5⁴ = 0.0625 even if every TA is tolerated. That is not a genome-wide essentiality claim.

steps.title: What to do
steps.body: Report occupancy and TA count. Use a method that models small genes conservatively, or treat the locus as uncertain. CRISPRi or a longer homologue comparison may be the evidence, not a starred Gumbel on n_TA = 4.

steps.title: Do not paste into a DST report
steps.body: Essentiality is not rpoB. A clinical isolate’s LOF in this gene is still a BAM question, not a TRANSIT p-value pasted into WHO grading.

example.takeaway: TnSeq is a saturated insertion likelihood. Small genes and bottlenecks are the regularity failures.

check.prompt: Himar1 TnSeq in Mtb primarily reports fitness at which sequence motif?
check.why: Himar1’s insertion specificity is TA. Saturation is counted in TA space, not in amino acids.

whyWrong.Start codons only: ATG is not the insertion motif.
whyWrong.PE_PGRS repeats exclusively: Those genes are hard to map; they are not the transposon’s motif.

check.prompt: A gene with 3 TA sites in a library with independent occupancy 0.5 per TA (toy model). P(all three empty | tolerated) is:
check.why: 0.5³ = 0.125. Empty is not automatic essentiality when n_TA is tiny.

whyWrong.0.875: That is 1 − 0.125, the chance of at least one insertion.

check.prompt: On the gene track, a cold N-terminal segment next to a hot C-terminus is the picture of:
choices: Domain-level (HMM) essentiality: part of the gene is required in this condition, not necessarily every codon
Proof that the gene is non-essential everywhere
check.answer: Domain-level (HMM) essentiality: part of the gene is required in this condition, not necessarily every codon
check.why: TRANSIT’s HMM was built for this pattern. A binary gene call would lie about the C-terminus.
